note.text: Description selects details to create a coherent impression for a reader. Organise attention, for example from entrance to interior or from a broad view to a significant object. Sensory detail should serve the intended mood rather than accumulate unrelated adjectives. Concrete nouns and precise verbs can carry description. A comparison should clarify an impression without making an unsupported literal claim. Avoid shifting viewpoint or time accidentally.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to create an impression through selected sensory detail and coherent organisation. Builds on: modification, comparison and narrative viewpoint. Leads to: later extended description and stylistic analysis.

paper_task.prompt: Describe a familiar shared space at a particular moment for a reader who has never seen it. Establish a viewpoint and a controlling impression, use an intelligible spatial order and select details that support the effect. Create a new passage rather than copying the reading-room model.
model: From the doorway, the reading room looked almost empty. A strip of afternoon light crossed the nearest table, leaving the far shelves in shadow. The open window lifted the edge of a loose page, then let it fall with a soft tap.

Beyond the table, a chair stood angled towards the window. Its worn seat and the small stack of folded notes beside it suggested recent use. I stopped at the threshold; the room seemed quiet rather than abandoned.
checklist: Controlling impression: the main effect towards which descriptive details contribute.
Spatial organisation: an order guiding attention through a described space.
Sensory detail: a specific impression associated with perception.
Qualified interpretation: a judgement limited to what observed detail suggests.
Use relevant original details and check sentence boundaries, agreement and spelling.
